_readme: COMMITTED SNAPSHOT of the catalog contract surface, generated from a real
migrated database and never hand-typed. Regenerate with:
node scripts/check-catalog-contract-checks.mjs --write   (DATABASE_URL pointed at a migrated DB)
FOUR sections are COMPARED against the database, each added because
something got through the previous set:
constraints      -- CHECKs on the five contract tables, with the function
bodies they call and the column types they constrain
foreignKeys      -- FKs incl. `wines` (a removed FK can reopen a hole
another constraint appears to cover)
generatedColumns -- expressions AND fold body hashes
styleVocabulary  -- category_styles pairs; a cross-side precondition
contractVersion is NOT one of them: it is workflow metadata, never compared,
surfaced only by --write when a `contract`-scoped constraint changes. Listing
it as a compared section was wrong and is the kind of miscount this file
exists to prevent elsewhere.
The gate (scripts/check-catalog-contract-checks.mjs, wired into check-schema.yml)
diffs this against pg_get_constraintdef on a freshly-migrated database and FAILS
the build on any difference. A predicate change is therefore impossible to ship
silently -- which is the whole point: 20260725220000 changed four of these from
btrim(x) <> '' to catalog_fold_v1(x) <> '' with no surface at all.
'scope' is the rejection-surface test from docs/dev/proposals/wine-catalog.md
§ Catalog write ownership: a constraint is CONTRACT iff a payload valid under the
old predicate can be REJECTED under the new one. 'contract' constraints require a
contract version bump + an announcement to the catalog-maintenance side.
'structural' ones are internal lifecycle invariants no conforming payload can
violate; they still get diffed (drift is drift) but changing one is not a
contract event.
'predicateDeps' records every FUNCTION a predicate calls, with a hash of its
definition, resolved via pg_depend. Without it the gate is blind one level down:
replacing gtin_check_digit_ok's body changes which barcodes are accepted while
the constraint reprints byte-identically (measured -- it passed the first version
of this gate). An ABSENT predicateDeps on a function-backed constraint FAILS the
gate rather than passing: absent means unverified, not none.
Changing a predicate: update the migration, re-run --write, and state the reason
in the PR. The gate does not care WHY -- it only guarantees nobody is surprised.
🔒 --write RESETS a changed constraint's scope to UNCLASSIFIED, and the gate then
fails until a human re-scopes it. That is deliberate: the rejection-surface test
is a property of a TRANSITION, not a permanent label, so a structural constraint
edited into a rejecting one must be re-judged rather than inheriting its old scope.
'generatedColumns' is the same protection for the five folded columns, which have
the blind spot in a worse form: generation_expression records the CALL, so a fold
body swap re-keys every row written afterwards while the expression is byte-
identical -- and Postgres never recomputes STORED values, so old and new rows
disagree with no error. Measured: 'Château X' stored 'CHÂTEAU X' after a swap.
Note grapes_folded depends on catalog_fold_arr_v1, which NO check constraint
references -- it was uncovered until this block existed. Absent block = FAIL.
🔒 'foldDependent' is DERIVED from predicateDeps, never carried. It used to be
copied forward and dropped on change, silently shedding the fold warning. A
property that is copied can desync from what it describes; a derived one cannot.
🔒 Every claim this gate makes has a STAGED FAILURE behind it (see the RFC).
If you add a behaviour here, stage its failure first -- that method is what found
the foldDependent bug, which review and reasoning had both passed over.

constraints.name: producers_status_check
constraints.definition: CHECK (((status)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['provisional'::character varying, 'confirmed'::character varying, 'linked'::character varying, 'archived'::character varying, 'rejected'::character varying])::text[])))

constraints.name: wine_products_status_check
